lab.Cargo.toml:
[workspace]
resolver = "3"
members = ["adder", "tiny", "bindgen", "wasi", "gotcha"]

# `cargo build --profile small`: the same code, built for size.
[profile.small]
inherits = "release"
opt-level = "z"
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
strip = true
lab.setup.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Installs one prebuilt tool into /usr/local/bin. Needs network. The versions are pinned here.
set -eu
GH=https://github.com
case "$1" in
  wasm-bindgen)
    v=0.2.129
    curl -sSfL "$GH/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen/releases/download/$v/wasm-bindgen-$v-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz" |
      tar xz -C /usr/local/bin --strip-components=1 "wasm-bindgen-$v-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl/wasm-bindgen"
    ;;
  wasmtime)
    v=v50.0.0
    curl -sSfL "$GH/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/releases/download/$v/wasmtime-$v-aarch64-linux.tar.xz" |
      tar xJ -C /usr/local/bin --strip-components=1 "wasmtime-$v-aarch64-linux/wasmtime"
    ;;
  wasm-opt)
    v=version_133
    curl -sSfL "$GH/WebAssembly/binaryen/releases/download/$v/binaryen-$v-aarch64-linux.tar.gz" |
      tar xz -C /usr/local --strip-components=1 "binaryen-$v/bin/wasm-opt" "binaryen-$v/lib"
    ;;
  wasm-pack)
    v=v0.15.0
    curl -sSfL "$GH/wasm-bindgen/wasm-pack/releases/download/$v/wasm-pack-$v-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz" |
      tar xz -C /usr/local/bin --strip-components=1 "wasm-pack-$v-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl/wasm-pack"
    ;;
  wasmer)
    v=v7.5.0
    curl -sSfL "$GH/wasmerio/wasmer/releases/download/$v/wasmer-linux-aarch64.tar.gz" |
      tar xz -C /usr/local/bin --strip-components=1 bin/wasmer
    ;;
  *) echo "unknown tool: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

gotcha.title: `std` compiles for the target, then the call fails
gotcha.looks_fine: `Command::output` and `thread::Builder::spawn` are ordinary `std` functions. They compile for the WebAssembly target as they do for your own machine, and the run on Linux or macOS succeeds.
gotcha.rust_sees: The standard library is present on `wasm32-wasip1`, but there the rustc book says spawning a thread or a process always returns an error (a separate `wasm32-wasip1-threads` target exists for threads; I did not run it). Both functions return `Err` (`ErrorKind::Unsupported`) instead of failing to compile, because their signatures already allow an error. The compiler checked the types, not what the target can do.
gotcha.why: The rustc book's page for the target says that "spawning a thread will always return an error" and "spawning a process will always return an error", while operations such as opening a file call the WASI functions. The page for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` says `std::thread::spawn` will panic there. The fix is to treat the error as an answer for that target: check for `ErrorKind::Unsupported`, and do the work on the calling thread or ask the host.
